newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT HITS NEW LOW AS IRAQ SALES DEADLINE LOOMS.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT HITS NEW LOW AS IRAQ SALES DEADLINE LOOMS.

text.p: IPE Brent crude hit fresh intra-day lows on Friday afternoon as persistent pressure from impending Iraqi oil exports continued to bear down on prices.
September Brent was down 16 cents at $18.74 a barrel at 1425 GMT after puncturing a technical support area around $18.75 to $18.75.
The market hit a new intra-day low of $18.71 at 1400 GMT.
"The market is still weak. People are holding back a bit for the deadline for Iraqi sales," said a broker who saw next technical support at $18.73.
The United Nations sanctions committee has until 1500 GMT on Friday to raise any objections to the price formula submitted by Iraq for selling its oil.
If no objections are raised Iraq can automatically resume selling oil under its oil-for-food deal with the U.N.
Meanwhile, the underlying Brent cargo market was also weak with prompt talking some 20 cents below September and short-dated swaps falling.
Falling gasoline prices have also undermined the value of Brent with prices losing some $20 a tonne over the past few days.
IPE gas oil was down $2.25 at $170.25 a tonne at 1421 GMT but dealers said there was good demand for diesel cargoes into France.
Dealers pegged support around $165 and some said poor demand from Germany for barge material could pull prices lower.
